Control settings for trop()

Source: R/trop.R
trop_control.Rd

Control settings for trop()

Usage

trop_control(
  max_iter = 2000L,
  tol = 1e-06,
  n_cv_cells = 120L,
  cv_cycles = 2L,
  max_cells = 60L,
  time_center = c("midpoint", "python"),
  pooled_treat_distance = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  n_boot = 200L,
  boot_resample = c("stratified", "controls"),
  boot_ci = c("percentile", "normal"),
  svd = c("truncated", "full"),
  cv_method = c("loocv", "placebo"),
  n_placebo = 30L,
  nn_floor = "auto",
  nn_floor_scale = 0.001,
  workers = 1L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

max_iter

Maximum solver iterations. Higher by default because small lambda_nn converges slowly under the soft-impute iteration.

tol

Reference solver convergence tolerance. The applied tolerance is tightened automatically as lambda_nn weakens (small penalties converge slowly), keeping accuracy roughly constant across the penalty grid; a fixed tolerance otherwise under-converges at small lambda_nn. See trop().

n_cv_cells

Number of control cells sampled for the CV criterion. Set to Inf (or 0) to use every control cell, i.e. the paper's full eq. (5) criterion (the Stata command's cells(0)); slower but exact.

cv_cycles

Number of coordinate-descent cycles in penalty selection.

max_cells

Threshold for anchor = "auto" to switch to pooled weights.

time_center

Where the pooled time weights theta_s = exp(-lambda_time |s - c|) are centred within a treated spell (anchor = "pooled", the placebo CV criterion and the pooled counterfactual behind the plots / event study). "midpoint" (default) uses the true midpoint c = (first + last) / 2 of the spell, the convention of the official Stata command (v0.2.4+); for a single treated period it reduces to the paper's per-cell distance |s - t|, so a single treated cell gets the same estimate under both anchors. "python" places the centre half a period later ((first + last + 1) / 2), the T - tp/2 convention of the official Python package, which trop_matrix() always uses; choose it for like-for-like comparisons with that package.

pooled_treat_distance

Optional overrides for the distances of a pooled group to itself, as a list with elements unit and/or time (single non-negative numbers; NULL, the default, keeps the usual distances). unit replaces the unit distance of every member of the group – which is otherwise its distance to the group average, hence generally non-zero with several members – by the given value, so list(unit = 0) gives the treated units the full unit weight; time replaces the time distance of the periods inside the spell by the given value, so list(time = 0) gives the treated periods the full time weight. This is the pooled_treat_distance(unit(#) time(#)) option of the official Stata command (v0.2.6+); it applies to the pooled anchor, the placebo-CV criterion and the pooled counterfactual behind the plots / event study, and is ignored by the per-cell anchor.

conf_level

Confidence level for intervals.

n_boot

Number of replications for the bootstrap standard error (se = "bootstrap").

boot_resample

Which units the bootstrap resamples: "stratified" (default) draws the treated and the control units separately, each with replacement (the stratified block bootstrap of the paper and of the Stata command); "controls" keeps the treated units fixed and resamples only the control units (the default resample = "controls" of the official Python package's trop.bootstrap, v0.1.11+, suited to designs with a single or very few treated units).

boot_ci

Bootstrap confidence-interval type: "percentile" or "normal".

svd

Singular-value decomposition used by the soft-impute solver: "truncated" (default) computes only the leading singular triplets with RSpectra when it is installed and the matrix is large enough to benefit, falling back to the full SVD otherwise; "full" always uses the exact base R svd(). The two agree to numerical tolerance; "truncated" is faster on large panels, "full" is used for exact numerical-agreement checks.

cv_method

Penalty cross-validation criterion. "loocv" (default) scores held-out control-cell prediction error (the paper's eq. (4)-(5)); "placebo" instead stamps the actual treated-unit adoption patterns onto randomly resampled control units and minimises the mean squared placebo ATT (the placebo-RMSE / pattern-resampling criterion of the official Python and Stata packages). Under block adoption the two placebo variants coincide; under staggered adoption each placebo draw reproduces the real cohort structure, so "placebo" is the recommended choice there (a warning is emitted if "loocv" is used on a staggered design). Ignored when the penalties are supplied via lambda (CV is then skipped). The placebo criterion always uses the pooled (per-cohort block-centre, cell-weighted) ATT, even when the final fit uses anchor = "per_cell".

n_placebo

Number of placebo assignments drawn when cv_method = "placebo" (larger is more stable but slower).

nn_floor

Small non-negative stabilising constant added to every finite lambda_nn inside the solver (lambda_nn = Inf, the DID/TWFE special case, is never affected). Rationale: the nuclear-norm proximal step soft-thresholds singular values by lambda_nn / (2 max w), so at lambda_nn = 0 the step degenerates to the identity, the completion of the treated cells is no longer pinned down by the program, and soft-impute converges slowly; a strictly positive floor keeps the weak-regularisation limit well posed. The default "auto" resolves to nn_floor_scale * s1, where s1 is the operator norm (largest singular value) of the two-way-demeaned control outcome – the same data-scale reference the default lambda_nn grid is built from. The floor is therefore relative to the outcome scale: it is resolved on the fitting scale, so it adapts automatically when standardize = TRUE (both modes get the same floor in relative terms). Supply a single non-negative number to use that exact value instead (interpreted on the fitting scale, like lambda), or 0 to disable the adjustment entirely, in which case penalties are applied exactly as given – use nn_floor = 0 for like-for-like numerical comparisons against other implementations at identical penalty values. The resolved value is stored in the fit as $lambda$nn_floor and printed when positive.

nn_floor_scale

Relative constant used when nn_floor = "auto": the resolved floor is nn_floor_scale * s1 (default 1e-3, i.e. 0.1\ data's operator norm – an epsilon next to the default lambda_nn grid, whose smallest finite point is 0.04 * s1). Ignored when nn_floor is numeric.

workers

Number of parallel workers for the embarrassingly parallel loops (cross-validation cells, and the bootstrap / jackknife replicates). 1 (default) runs serially. Values > 1 use future.apply/future when installed (a transient multisession plan is set up and restored automatically); if those packages are missing it falls back to serial with no error. Results are reproducible given seed.

seed

Optional seed for CV cell sampling (reproducibility).

Value

A list of control parameters.
